_why_overrides_workbench_base: Fix round 1 (Task 4 review). The first version of this file shipped
`overrides: []`, reasoned from the wrong scope: every rule below is
`subtree`, and `no_two_components_claim_one_destination_without_declaring_it`
only polices `file` rules, so nothing here was ever a *rule-level*
collision needing a declaration. But `overrides` is not read by that test
alone — a later stage reads it at the *file* level, to tell a BoingBag
deliberately replacing a file from `declared_by_the_owner_component` from
a genuine surprise. Measured directly against the owner's real media
(Task 4 review): every one of BoingBag 3.9-1's 210 files sits at a path
the base AmigaOS 3.9 recipe's `workbench-base` component already writes —
100%, not merely 'some'. Leaving `overrides` empty made that whole
measured fact invisible to whatever reads it, which is worse than not
declaring anything: a constant `declared: false` on every one of a
BoingBag's rows tells a reader nothing, which is exactly the noise this
field exists to separate a real surprise from (spec §3).
`recipe.rs`'s `every_override_names_a_component_that_exists` originally
could not resolve this anyway: it checked `recipe.component(over)` against
the one-component pseudo-`Recipe` `shipped_recipes()` built for a package,
which never contains `workbench-base` — a different recipe's component
entirely. Fixed there (Task 4 review) by resolving `over` against the
union of every shipped id, releases and packages together, rather than
one recipe's own list — see `all_shipped_component_ids` in `recipe.rs`.
name: BoingBag 3.9-1
_why_host_placement_block: ART-166, measured in Task 8's real run and confirmed three independent
ways (ART's own reader, 7-Zip 26.02, the raw general-purpose flag word
0x0003 with bit 0 set): the `AmigaOS-Update` member named above is a
ZIP whose every entry is ZipCrypto-encrypted — 233 of 233 entries in
3.9-1's payload, 147 of 147 in 3.9-2's. The password belongs to the
BoingBag's own `Updater`, which the wrapper LHA carries beside the
payload and which has to run *on* an Amiga; every established
distribution builder (HstWB Installer, AmiKit, AmigaSYS, ClassicWB)
installs a BoingBag by running that Updater inside an emulator rather
than by decrypting anything, and the owner's recorded decision is that
So the rules below are right and unreachable, and spec §10/§89 says ART
must not offer what it cannot do. Declaring the block here — data, not
code — is what makes the screen refuse the tick with a translated
sentence naming the Updater, instead of accepting it and meeting the
reader's own raw English `Password required to decrypt file` after the
user already confirmed. The day the Amiga-side install round lands,
this one key is deleted and nothing else changes.
